title: Delegated sync: nested-group depth causes RBAC v2 role-resolution regression and stale session cache leads to transient permission mismatch
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Several customers reported intermittent 'permission denied' errors for users who should have admin or collaborator access immediately after a scheduled group-sync job. In parallel we observed a small set of cases where non-admin service tokens temporarily retained elevated access. The behavior was reproduced in-house and traced to two interacting regressions in RBAC v2: (1) the role-resolution algorithm changed heuristics for deeply nested groups (depth > 5) causing non-deterministic fallback ordering when computing effective grants; (2) the session-role cache did not flush appropriately after group-sync updates, so stale role mappings persisted for up to cache_TTL and led to both over-permission and under-permission windows. Impact: high for customers performing bulk migrations or frequent group-sync schedules (SAML/SCIM setups).
steps_to_reproduce: Create org with nested groups: team-A -> group-1 -> subgroup-1 -> subgroup-2 -> subgroup-3 -> subgroup-4 (depth 6)
Map subgroup-4 to 'project-admin' role via SAML/SCIM group attribute mapping
Run scheduled group-sync job every 5 minutes (customer-configured) while simultaneously rotating a service integration token used for cross-tenant migration
Observe: some user sessions show 'permission denied' when calling project admin endpoints immediately after sync, while a small fraction of service tokens retain admin grants beyond expected window
Check audit logs: missing role-resolution breakdown event and no explicit session-flush recorded
observed_logs_and_errors: Examples from customer logs: 'rbac: role resolution fallback used: raw-group-order' and 'session-cache: hit stale-role-map' plus HTTP 403 for /v1/projects/:id/admin endpoints. Audit events lacked a detailed 'role_resolution_path' field which makes root cause analysis harder for support.
root_cause: Regression introduced in the 'flatten-and-sort' optimization for RBAC v2 (commit 7f3a9c) made the algorithm use a non-deterministic hash when group-nesting exceeded 5 layers. That produced inconsistent grant ordering that in rare cases let a less privileged mapping shadow a privileged one. Separately, the session-role cache was only invalidated by explicit user re-login or a full identity refresh; group-sync path used an async updater that did not emit a session-flush event. The combination produced windows where either permissions dropped or stale elevated permissions remained.
resolution: 1) Revert non-deterministic flatten heuristic and replace with deterministic DFS ordering for nested groups, with an explicit depth cap check and deterministic tie-breaker. 2) Emit 'session_role_flush' events from group-sync job on any role-affecting delta and make the session cache listen to the event to purge affected session keys. 3) Add a new audit event type 'role_resolution_path' that includes the deterministic ancestry chain used to grant roles so support can reproduce mappings. 4) Short-term mitigation: backfill a one-off force-flush for customer orgs that reported impact.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind 'rbac_v2_nested_fix' flag. Canary: 10% of runtime hosts for 24h with synthetic group-sync churn tests and two impacted customer orgs opted into canary. Monitor: role_mismatch_count, session_cache_miss_rate, and 403_rate_for_admin_endpoints. If green, ramp to 100% over 48h. Post-deploy: run a force session-flush job for all orgs that have had group-sync activity in the last 72h.
test_plan: Unit tests for DFS deterministic ordering with randomized group graphs. Integration tests: SCIM/SAML group-sync pipeline with session-cache invalidation assertions. E2E: reproduce customer scenario in staging with scheduled sync every 1m and a migration service token churn. Add audit log assertions for 'role_resolution_path'. Add chaos test that injects group mapping deltas during high concurrency to ensure no over-permission windows.
comments: 2026-01-11 - Asha Patel: Triage call with support and SRE. Identified reproducer and confirmed customer impact windows. Created staging repro org.
2026-01-15 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented deterministic DFS ordering and added tie-breaker using stable group id. Draft PR submitted for review (see links).
2026-01-20 - Sofia Martinez (Security Review): Reviewed algorithm change — approved but requested additional audit fields and a guardrail to reject overly deep mapping by default.
2026-01-25 - Devops: Added session-flush hook to group-sync pipeline. Deployed to staging and validated that sessions are purged when role deltas applied.
2026-01-29 - QA: Ran synthetic churn test for 24h. Observed 95% reduction in transient 403s and no over-permission cases in staging. A few flaky cases remain in the edge simulator.
2026-02-02 - Customer Success: Notified affected customers about planned maintenance and canary opt-in. Two customers accepted canary testing.
2026-02-03 - Liam O'Connor: Merged PR after one minor doc change. Preparing canary deployment.
2026-02-03 - Asha Patel: Marking for In Review; will monitor canary metrics and finalize rollout notes.
post_mortem_notes: We will add an engineering practice to include deterministic ordering tests for any optimization that changes iteration over user/group trees. Also adding a dashboard tile to show 'audit events without role_resolution_path' so support can spot missing context quickly. Schedule a follow-up to evaluate lowering default group-sync frequency guidance for customers doing heavy nested mappings.
